ImageDescription.value: Statues of (from left to right) en:Sang Nila Utama, a pseudo-legendary Prince from en:Palembang who supposedly founded the en:Kingdom of Singapura, en:Munshi Abdullah, a Malay linguist in the employ of Sir Stamford Raffles who would come to be known as the "Father of Modern Malay Literature", en:Tan Tock Seng, a prominent Chinese entrepreneur and philanthropist, Sir en:Stamford Raffles, founder of the British colony of Singapore, and en:Naraina Pillai, a leader of the Indian community in the colony of Singapore and contributor to the en:Sri Mariamman Temple, Singapore. All statues save for that of Sir Stamford Raffles were erected at the en:Raffles Landing Site as part of events commemorating the bicentennial of Singapore's colonisation by the en:British East India Company.

These images were mostly created as Color slides in the second half of the 20th century.

Setup:

A holding devise for slides and negatives is set over flat lightbox. This setup ensures that the setup stays stable when manually replacing slides.

The camera (Sony α 6600), equiped with a macro-lens (Sony FE 50mm F2.8 Macro )is mounted inversely on a tripod to utilize the full potential of the macro-lens.

Since the α 6600 has an APS-C-sensor the display-ratio is 1:1.4 and not 1:1.

To ensure a shock-free exposure a remote control via smart-phone-app was used.

Images with the template {{User:Rainer Halama/Photodigitization}} will be inserted in the category Photo-digitized Images by User:Rainer Halama.
